_meta.indication: BYSTOLIC is indicated for the treatment of hypertension, alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents
_meta.receipt_date: Originally submitted April 30, 2004 (resubmitted May 30 and December 5, 2007)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled monotherapy trials (Studies 1, 2, and 3), plus a fourth placebo-controlled add-on trial (Study 4)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Not specified by phase; randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-group dose-ranging studies
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multi-center, placebo-controlled, parallel-group dose-ranging trials; patients received BYSTOLIC or placebo once daily for twelve weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with mild to moderate hypertension with baseline diastolic blood pressures (DBP) of 95 to 109 mmHg; Study 3 enrolled only Black patients
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Placebo-subtracted least-square mean reduction in trough sitting diastolic (and systolic) blood pressure
pivotal_trials.n: 2016 patients across the three monotherapy trials (1811 BYSTOLIC, 205 placebo); the add-on Study 4 enrolled 669 patients
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant, generally dose-related placebo-subtracted least-square mean reductions in trough sitting systolic/diastolic BP; diastolic reductions by dose: Study 1 -5.1 (1.25 mg) to -8.3 mmHg (30-40 mg); Study 2 -3.2 to -4.5 mmHg; Study 3 (Black patients) -2.9 to -6.1 mmHg; Study 4 (add-on) -3.3 to -4.6 mmHg (* p<0.05 vs placebo)

key_safety: Most common treatment-emergent adverse events (incidence >=1% and > placebo) included headache (9% at 5 mg vs 6% placebo), fatigue (up to 5% at 20-40 mg vs 1% placebo), dizziness (up to 4% vs 2% placebo), diarrhea, and nausea; the most common signs of overdose were bradycardia and hypotension
target_moa: Nebivolol is a beta-adrenergic receptor blocking agent that is preferentially beta-1 selective in extensive metabolizers at doses <=10 mg; the antihypertensive mechanism has not been definitively established but may involve decreased heart rate, decreased myocardial contractility, suppression of renin activity, and vasodilation
modality: Small molecule (nebivolol, a racemic selective beta-1 receptor antagonist; new molecular entity)

advisory_committee.vote: NDA 21-742 was not referred to an advisory committee because there are several previously approved agents in the beta-blocker class, the safety data revealed no unexpected issues for the class, and the efficacy trials posed no particular concerns

description.text: Converted labeling to Physician Labeling Rule (PLR) format with editorial/safety labeling changes; no new indication or population added.

citations.quote: This supplemental new drug application provides for conversion to the Physician Labeling Rule Format (PLR) and changes to the **DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION, WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, ADVERSE EVENTS, USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS, OVERDOSAGE, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY**, and the **PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION** sections of the label.

summary.text: Standard NDA (505(b)(1)) for nebivolol, a new molecular entity selective beta-1 blocker, for hypertension; the application originally submitted April 30, 2004 received an Approvable action in 2005 over mouse Leydig cell tumors, and was approved December 17, 2007 after a complete response, without referral to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) originally submitted April 30, 2004, and resubmitted May 30 and December 5, 2007 under section 505(b)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for nebivolol 2.5, 5, and 10 mg Tablets.
Nebivolol is a selective \beta_1 receptor antagonist and a new molecular entity.
On May 31, 2005, NDA 21-742 for Nevibolol Tablets received an “Approvable” action. The “Approvable” deficiency was:

NDA 21-742 was not referred to an advisory committee for review because there are several previously approved agents in the \beta-blocker class of drugs, evaluation of the safety data did not reveal particular safety issues that were unexpected for this class, and the design and results of the efficacy trials did not pose particular concerns.

requirement.text: Conduct a placebo-controlled withdrawal study following at least three months of treatment (Final Protocol by 04/2008, Study Start by 10/2008, Final Report by 12/2010)

citations.quote: 1. Conduct a placebo-controlled withdrawal study following at least three months of treatment.

date.text: Approvable (not Complete Response) action issued May 31, 2005; a subsequent approvable letter was issued November 30, 2007

citations.quote: On May 31, 2005, NDA 21-742 for Nevibolol Tablets received an “Approvable” action. The “Approvable” deficiency was:
The December 5, 2007 submission constituted a complete response to our November 30, 2007 approvable letter.

basis.text: The outstanding issue preventing approval was the observation that male mice developed Leydig cell tumors and hyperplasia during chronic treatment with nebivolol

citations.quote: The one outstanding issue that prevented approval of nebivolol during the original review cycle was the observation that male mice developed Leydig cell tumors and hyperplasia during chronic treatment with nebivolol.
